newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude weaker, hopes for Dubai diffs to fall.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude weaker, hopes for Dubai diffs to fall.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower on Friday as futures dropped overnight, amid continued discount trading of MidEast and regional crudes.
Traders reported a Murban cargo changing hands at ADNOC -4/5 cents between Japanese players and a separate Murban being traded at ADNOC -10/15 cents from a Japanese trader to a European major.

Lower Zakum was also said traded at ADNOC -7/10 cents between U.S. majors. But, a European major was also said to have sold a partial of Umm Shaif at ADNOC +7 cents and a partial of Murban at ADNOC +1 cent.

However, sellers took little cheer from the premium deals. A handful of Dubai and Oman cargoes were still available, and on the lighter grades three Qatar Marine cargoes and some ADNOC grades were still available.
They said they expected some slow down in trading pending the release next week of official selling prices from Middle East governments to help bring prices back into line.

In addition, India was scheduled to award its April buying tender this weekend, which could absorb some of the available Dubai cargoes. Traders said that five or six Dubai cargoes had been offered into the tender.
U.N. sources said overnight that IOC had signed up to take 40,000 barrels of Iraqi crude over 90 days, which could start to impact its monthly tender demand.
Regional grades remained well supplied and few bids were seen in the market. Traders estimated well over 1.0 million barrels of Minas were still available.
A Duri trade was talked at ICP -50 cents, matching a day-earlier Minas price and traders said they expected a further price decline before Indonesian grades were more competitive.
